# Troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

## Containers Exit or Docker Runs Out of Memory

Each service has a memory limit, listed on its [profile page](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/profiles/index.md). The limits of everything you start add up, and Docker needs that much memory available. Give Docker the memory that [Getting Started](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/#requirements) names, start fewer profiles at once, or choose a lite profile over a full one. To lower a limit, edit `mem_limit` in the compose file in `.odctl` and run `odctl recreate <profile>`, as [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) shows for SeaweedFS.

## Uploads Fail with HTTP 500 and Seaweed Exited with Code 137

`seaweed` reached its memory limit while it buffered a large upload, and the kernel killed it. The client sees HTTP 500 and every profile that uses S3 loses its storage until the container starts again. `docker inspect seaweed --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'` prints `true` after such a kill. A model or file of several hundred MB can reach the limit. Raise `mem_limit` and `GOMEMLIMIT` together, as [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) shows for 2 GB. A workspace made by a release before `GOMEMLIMIT` was added lacks it until you run `odctl init --force`, which [Start Again](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#start-again) describes.

## A Port Is Already in Use

Every service publishes fixed host ports, listed on its profile page. If another program holds one, `odctl up` fails to start that service. Stop the other program, or change the host side of the port mapping in `.odctl/compose-*.yml` and run `odctl recreate <profile>`, as [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) shows for Trino. Containers still reach each other on their internal ports, so only clients on your host need the new port.

## Use 127.0.0.1, Not localhost

Host addresses in `odctl explain` and on these pages use `127.0.0.1`. With IPv6 enabled in Docker, `localhost` can resolve to a service's IPv6 address, and services that listen on IPv4 only reset the connection. `localhost` works when Docker's IPv6 is off.

## No Published Image for a TAG

`odctl up` checks the images odctl builds before it starts anything. If the registry says an image for the resolved `TAG` does not exist, it stops with `No published image for TAG=...` and lists the missing images. An image already on your machine passes without a registry call. If the registry cannot be reached, odctl starts anyway and Docker reports what it finds.

The usual causes are a CLI version whose images are not published yet, or a `TAG` in `.odctl/.env` that you changed by hand. Set `TAG` to a published version in `.odctl/.env`, or install a CLI version whose images exist.

## Workspace TAG Differs from the CLI Version

After you upgrade the CLI, every command except `odctl init` warns that `.odctl/.env` sets an older `TAG`. The workspace keeps the old profiles, images and compose files until you run `odctl init --force`. [Start Again](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#start-again) says what that command removes.

## A Service Is Up but Does Not Work

`odctl logs <profile>` shows the logs of a profile's containers. Add `-s <service>` for one service, or `-f` to follow them. `odctl ps --all` shows every container odctl manages and its state.

## Older Messages Are Missing

The Kafka brokers delete old messages, so a consumer that starts from the beginning of a topic sees only what is left. [Keep Messages Longer](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/kafka/#keep-messages-longer) gives the limits, shows how to read them and shows how to set `retention.ms` and `retention.bytes` to `-1` on a topic that must keep everything.
# About

# Why odctl

I like building demo apps, and each one needs a local environment to try things in. Docker and Docker Compose are good for that. Across several projects, though, it is not easy, and the setup drifts from one project to the next.

odctl is a CLI that manages Docker Compose services. It runs Compose files and selects services with Compose profiles. For one small project with two or three services, plain Compose is fine.

It starts to hurt when you have several projects. One needs Kafka, Flink and Iceberg. Another needs Spark and Trino but not Kafka. Each project ends up with its own Compose file, and over time they drift apart, for example when you upgrade image tags in one and forget the others. With odctl, the files live in one place. Each release fixes the image versions, and an end-to-end test runs every profile before it is published. A project just pins an odctl version.

The second part is the wiring, and odctl does it for you. When PostgreSQL first starts, it creates a database for each service that needs one, such as the Iceberg catalog, Airflow and MLflow. The Iceberg REST catalog keeps its tables in S3 storage (SeaweedFS), and Spark and Trino are already configured to use it. Kafka Connect, Flink and Spark also need connector jars with matching versions. odctl builds them once into a shared image, and each service takes the jars it needs from there. `odctl up spark-lite` starts PostgreSQL, the storage, the catalog and the shared jars first, and Prometheus already scrapes Kafka, Flink, Spark and ClickHouse.

The third part is day-to-day use. With several Compose files, it is hard to remember what is running and where. odctl has commands for that:

- `odctl list` shows every profile and what it runs.
- `odctl explain spark-lite` shows a profile's services, images, ports and the profiles it depends on.
- `odctl up spark-lite --dry-run` shows what would start, in order, before anything starts.
- `odctl ps --all` lists the running containers and their ports.
- `odctl logs spark-lite` shows the logs of one profile.
- `odctl down --all` stops everything.

Getting all of this right by hand takes time, and it is easy to break across projects.

I use odctl in my own projects: [desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/) starts the services of its tests and examples with it, and so do the demos in [benchtop](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/benchtop). It is useful for three kinds of project:

- **Data engineering.** Streaming and batch pipelines on Kafka, Kafka Connect, Flink, Fluss and Spark, an Iceberg lakehouse queried with Trino, ClickHouse for analytics, Airflow and Temporal to run them, and lineage in Marquez and OpenMetadata.
- **ML and MLOps.** MLflow tracks experiments, registers models and serves them. Feast serves features from Iceberg tables and Valkey, and Evidently stores drift reports. The Airflow image has the MLflow and Feast clients, with the tracking URI and the Feast registry already set.
- **AI.** PostgreSQL has pgvector and pg_textsearch for [hybrid search](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/hybrid-search/index.md), and Valkey has vector search. An AI assistant can choose a profile and reach its services with the odctl skill and `llms.txt`, as [Getting started](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/#use-it-with-an-ai-assistant) describes. The [Roadmap](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/roadmap/index.md) adds an MCP server for AI agents, a Langfuse profile for tracing LLM and agent applications, and a desflow server profile after desflow 1.0.

# Roadmap

The work comes in the order shown, without dates: a release ships when it is ready. Features come first, then the testing and setup work that adds no feature. Each planned item links to its GitHub issue where one exists.

## Next Releases

1.4.0: Feast

An MCP endpoint for agents, pushing streaming features and materialising from Airflow, and vector retrieval on PostgreSQL. [#150](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/150)

1.5.0: Stable interface and JSON output

A written list of what 1.x keeps stable: profile names, ports, `.env` keys, volumes and the workspace files. `--json` on `list`, `explain`, `ps` and `info`, and `--yes` on `init` and `down` for scripts. [#140](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/140)

1.6.0: MCP server

Tools for AI agents that show the profiles and what is running, with `up` and `down` behind a setting. [#141](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/141)

1.7.0: Langfuse

A profile for tracing and evaluating LLM and agent applications, using odctl's ClickHouse. [#120](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/120)

1.8.0: Snapshot and restore

`odctl snapshot` and `odctl restore` save a profile's data and bring it back, so a lab or an agent can start again from a known state. [#142](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/142)

1.9.0: Lineage and alerts

Lineage from Airflow, Spark and Feast in Marquez, and Grafana alert rules, starting with one for a failed DAG run. [#149](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/149)

1.10.0: Kafka Connect transforms

Transforms built into the Connect image: make a record schema required, replace personal fields with a hash, and send lineage events to Marquez for any connector. [#143](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/143)

1.11.0: Memory check and models on the host

`odctl up` warns when Docker has less memory than the profiles it starts need. One setting lets containers reach a model server on the host with an OpenAI-compatible API, such as Ollama or LM Studio, on macOS, Linux and WSL2. The guide also covers the Ollama embeddings route, batch embedding in Airflow and a hand-run rerank server. [#155](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/155), [#109](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/109)

MLOps guides

Guides for a prediction log and labels in PostgreSQL, feature and leakage checks, hyperparameter search, ONNX quantisation, serving a second model or many models, serving latency sent over OTLP, Feast dataset versions and reads of large Iceberg tables. No new service and no new version: the guides are published when they reach `main`.

Agents guides

Guides for traces, token metrics, feedback and evaluation of agent and model calls, an agent in a Temporal workflow, agent services beside the stack, and agent state in PostgreSQL. No new service and no new version.

Retrieval guides

Guides for hybrid search with rank fusion, graph queries in PostgreSQL, ingestion with change detection, Valkey as a cache, and media with signed URLs. No new service and no new version.

1.12.0: Label Studio

A `label-studio` profile for labelling data by hand, on odctl's PostgreSQL. Its guide loads the exported labels into the label table of the MLOps guides.

## Alongside

Work that does not wait for a release, published as it is ready.

- **Guides**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Iceberg table maintenance with Spark, vector search in Valkey, and traces and prompts in MLflow.

  [#152](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/152)

- **Testing and CI**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  It lands between 1.10.0 and 1.11.0. It changes only the tests, the CI workflows, the dependency update settings and two docs pages, not odctl itself, so it has no version of its own. The end-to-end tests run on every pull request, including image updates, so an update is tested before it merges. Each release is also tested as an upgrade from the one before it, and on arm64, which most Macs run. A pull request then tests only the profiles it changes, and the full suite runs every night. The CI user guide and the per-task environments section are published with 1.11.0.

  [#102](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/102)

## After desflow 1.0

- **desflow server**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  When the desflow server ships: a profile that runs the [desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/) simulation server, so a project can start simulations that write to Kafka, PostgreSQL or Iceberg.

  [#144](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/issues/144)

## Released

Newest first.

1.3.0: OpenMetadata connectors

Custom OpenMetadata connectors uploaded to S3 are picked up by the ingestion container with no restart, AutoPilot is off by default, extra packages can be installed in the ingestion container, and OpenMetadata runs 2.0.7.

1.2.2: newer images

Trino, Metabase, `otel-lgtm` and the PostgreSQL JDBC driver in the deps image are updated, and the Grafana dashboard descriptions no longer name the exact version of the component they show.

1.2.1: recreate on several files

`odctl recreate`, `odctl restart` and `odctl logs` work on profiles from more than one compose file, `odctl init` and `odctl down` can skip their prompt, and the docs show every command with a runnable example.

1.2.0: Streaming

Flink writes to HTTP APIs such as Feast's push endpoint, Spark reads Kafka without downloading packages, and new guides cover Kafka retention and several rolling windows in Flink SQL. The release also fixes the MLflow and storage guides and sets `GOMEMLIMIT`, a soft limit for the Go runtime, on `seaweed`, so large model uploads do not hit its container memory limit.

1.1.0: localhost-only services

Every service is reachable from your machine only, Kafka no longer publishes the minikube listener ports, an odctl skill and `llms.txt` help AI assistants, and the docs have this Roadmap and a [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/changelog/index.md).

1.0.2: Python 3.15

odctl is tested on Python 3.15, ZooKeeper and Metabase are updated, and Renovate groups image updates by compose file.

1.0.1: upgrade fixes

Old jars no longer stay in the shared deps volume after an upgrade, and without a workspace odctl's images run with odctl's own version instead of a cached `latest`.

1.0.0: documentation site and compatibility promise

A documentation site with guides, profile pages and the CLI reference. Semantic versioning with a compatibility promise for 1.x. `odctl up` works straight after `odctl recreate`.

What each release changed is in the [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/changelog/index.md) and on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/releases).

# Changelog

Each release, newest first: what changed, then under Upgrading what to change in commands, workspaces or clients that use the previous release. Releases up to 1.0.2 are described on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl/releases).

## Version 1.3.0

Custom connectors for OpenMetadata, extra packages for its ingestion container, AutoPilot off by default, OpenMetadata 2.0.7, and newer Kafka and Metabase images.

- A Python connector uploaded to `s3://openmetadata/connectors` is importable in the ingestion container within about 15 seconds, and a change to it is used by the next agent run with no restart. [Add a Custom Connector](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/openmetadata/#add-a-custom-connector) creates its service and agent through the API.
- OpenMetadata's AutoPilot, which creates and runs default agents for a service added in the UI, is off by default. The new `.env` key `METADATA_AUTOPILOT` turns it on, and the new `openmetadata-init` service applies it each time `metadata` starts. See [Register PostgreSQL as a Database Service](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/openmetadata/#register-postgresql-as-a-database-service).
- `_METADATA_PIP_DEPS` in `.odctl/.env` installs extra Python packages in the `openmetadata-ingestion` container, as `_AIRFLOW_PIP_DEPS` does for Airflow. See [Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples).
- `openmetadata-ingestion` has a healthcheck, so `odctl up` and `odctl recreate` return once its Airflow answers.
- [Where Data Lives](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#where-data-lives) shows the three profiles that read their code from a bucket: `airflow`, `feast` and `metadata`.
- OpenMetadata and its ingestion container run 2.0.7, up from 2.0.1.
- On a new database the sign-in domain is `odctl.io`, and a second admin `user@odctl.io` has the password `password`. The ingestion Airflow takes `user` and `password`.
- Kafka and Kafka Connect run `apache/kafka:4.3.2`, up from 4.3.1. Metabase runs v0.64.3.5, up from v0.64.3.1. The deps image has `log4j-slf4j2-impl` 2.26.1, up from 2.23.1.

### Upgrading

- The `metadata` profile now also starts `storage`, SeaweedFS on 127.0.0.1 ports 8333, 8889 and 9333, from which the ingestion container takes connectors.
- Two new `.env` keys, `_METADATA_PIP_DEPS` and `METADATA_AUTOPILOT`, are written by `odctl init`. An existing `.env` works without them: add the lines, or get them with `odctl init --force`.
- AutoPilot is now off unless `METADATA_AUTOPILOT="true"`, so a service added in the OpenMetadata UI no longer gets default agents. An existing `.env` has no key, which means off. Set `METADATA_AUTOPILOT="true"` in `.odctl/.env` to keep the old behaviour.
- `openmetadata-migrate` runs `openmetadata-ops.sh migrate` against your existing database on the next start of `metadata`, by `odctl up` or `odctl recreate`, for the move from 2.0.1 to 2.0.7. Going back to 2.0.1 afterwards is not tested.
- The sign-in domain `odctl.io` and the password `password` of `user` apply to a new database only. A database from an earlier release keeps its users `admin@open-data.local` and `user@open-data.local`, both with the password `admin`, because the server restores a user's stored email on every update (`UserRepository.java`, `entitySpecificUpdate`, at `2.0.7-release`) and keeps a stored password. On that database `admin@odctl.io` and `user@odctl.io` fail with HTTP 400, "You have entered an invalid username or password."
- The ingestion Airflow login changes from `admin` / `admin` to `user` / `password`.
- A workspace made by `odctl init` with an earlier release keeps its old `compose-metadata.yml`, `compose-infra.yml`, `compose-kafka.yml`, `compose-analytics.yml` and `registry.yml`, has no `openmetadata/connector_sync.py` or `openmetadata/autopilot_init.py`, and so has none of the changes above. Run `odctl init --force` to copy the new files; it replaces your edits, so keep a copy of them. Then run `odctl recreate metadata storage`, and `odctl recreate` for the Kafka and Metabase profiles you use, such as `odctl recreate kafka-lite metabase`.

## Version 1.2.2

Newer images for Trino, Metabase and the observability stack.

- Trino runs 484, up from 483. Metabase runs v0.64.3.1, up from v0.63.19.3. `otel-lgtm` runs `grafana/otel-lgtm:0.37.0`, up from 0.35.0. The deps image has the PostgreSQL JDBC driver 42.7.14, up from 42.7.13.
- The Grafana dashboard descriptions no longer name the exact version of the component they show, so they stay true when an image is updated. They name a major version only where it tells two kinds apart: Flink 2, whose metrics differ from Flink 1, and OpenMetadata 2, which is maintained beside OpenMetadata 1.

### Upgrading

- A workspace made by `odctl init` with an earlier release keeps its old compose files, and so the old images. Run `odctl init --force` to copy the new files; it replaces your edits, so keep a copy of them. Then run `odctl recreate` for the profiles you use, such as `odctl recreate trino metabase`.

## Version 1.2.1

`recreate`, `restart` and `logs` work on profiles from several compose files, `init` and `down` can skip their prompt, and the docs show every command with a runnable example.

- `odctl recreate`, `odctl restart` and `odctl logs` work on profiles from more than one compose file, such as `odctl recreate storage kafka-lite`. They ran every file as one project, so `recreate` failed with `Conflict. The container name "/seaweed" is already in use`, and `restart` and `logs` left out the containers of all but one file. Each file now runs as its own project, as with `odctl up`. [Apply a Change](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#apply-a-change) uses `odctl recreate`.
- `odctl init --force --yes` and `odctl down --all --volumes --yes` run without asking `Are you sure?`, for scripts and CI. `-y` is the short form. See [Stop a Profile](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/#stop-a-profile) and [Start Again](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#start-again).
- [Getting Started](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/index.md) runs every command on `kafka-lite`, with its output, and the [home page](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/#commands) lists each command with a link to its example.
- Every guide ends with a Runnable Example that names the files to run. [Rolling Windows](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/rolling-windows/index.md) is a page of its own, and the Flink push to Feast moved to [Push Features from Flink SQL](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/feast-iceberg/#push-features-from-flink-sql).
- The animation on [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#what-odctl-up-does) shows its four steps again. Since 1.1.0 it showed steps 1 to 3 for a moment each and then stayed on step 4, because one step was exported 2 pixels narrower and ffmpeg stopped at the change in size.
- The Labs page is hidden until its first lab is published.

## Version 1.2.0

Flink can send rows to an HTTP API, Spark reads Kafka with no extra options, SeaweedFS survives uploads of large models, and the guides cover cases that real projects met.

- Flink's SQL client has the HTTP connector. [Push Features from Flink SQL](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/feast-iceberg/#push-features-from-flink-sql) pushes a feature value to Feast.
- Spark has the Kafka connector and the Avro module, so a job reads a topic, including Avro records written with the schema registry, with no `--packages` option. See [Read a Kafka Topic](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/spark/#read-a-kafka-topic) and [Read Avro Records Written with the Schema Registry](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/spark/#read-avro-records-written-with-the-schema-registry).
- [Keep Messages Longer](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/kafka/#keep-messages-longer) shows the broker's one-day and 500 MB retention and how to turn both off for a topic. [Troubleshooting](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/troubleshooting/#older-messages-are-missing) lists the symptom.
- `seaweed` sets `GOMEMLIMIT` to three quarters of its memory limit, so uploads of a model of a few hundred MB no longer end with HTTP 500 and a killed container. [Troubleshooting](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/troubleshooting/#uploads-fail-with-http-500-and-seaweed-exited-with-code-137) says what to do when the limit is still reached, and [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) changes both values together.
- The [MLflow guide](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/mlflow/index.md) has three new sections: [Move the Alias to a New Version](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/mlflow/#move-the-alias-to-a-new-version), which needs `odctl restart mlflow`, [Load a Model from Your Machine](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/mlflow/#load-a-model-from-your-machine) and [Serve a Model That Reads Online Features](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/mlflow/#serve-a-model-that-reads-online-features).
- The docs now say that the packages in `_MLOPS_PIP_DEPS` are installed from PyPI again in every new `mlflow` and `mlflow-serve` container. [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) lists when a new container is made.
- [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#examples) shows how to create a bucket before its profile exists.
- [Rolling Windows](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/rolling-windows/index.md) shows that Flink SQL refuses two different `OVER` windows in one streaming query, and the two ways around it.
- The [Evidently guide](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/guides/evidently-reports/index.md) says what Evidently does not estimate and why NannyML needs Python 3.12.

### Upgrading

- A workspace made by `odctl init` with an earlier release keeps its old `compose-infra.yml`, which has no `GOMEMLIMIT` for `seaweed`. Run `odctl init --force` to copy the new files; it replaces your edits, so keep a copy of them. Then run `odctl recreate storage`.

## Version 1.1.0

Every service is now reachable from your machine only, and the docs have a [Roadmap](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/roadmap/index.md) and a [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/about/changelog/index.md).

- Every published port binds to `127.0.0.1`, on macOS, Linux and WSL2, so other machines on your network cannot reach the services. [How You Reach a Service](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/#how-you-reach-a-service) says how to open a port when you need to.
- Kafka no longer publishes ports 29092, 29093 and 29094, which were listeners for a minikube cluster.
- An odctl skill and `llms.txt` help an AI assistant choose a profile and reach its services. See [Use It with an AI Assistant](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/getting-started/#use-it-with-an-ai-assistant).
- Eight guides show in a diagram how data moves between their services, and [How It Works](https://jaehyeon.me/odctl/latest/how-it-works/index.md) shows what `odctl up` checks and the order it starts services in. The end-to-end tests run every command the guides show.
- The tables of `odctl ps` and `odctl explain` draw straight right borders on rows with port mappings.
- `odctl down --help` says what `--volumes` removes.

### Upgrading

- To reach a service from another machine, run `odctl init`, remove `127.0.0.1:` from the service's port line in `.odctl/compose-*.yml`, and run `odctl recreate <profile>`.
- A Kafka client in minikube cannot use `host.minikube.internal:29092` any more. Add a listener for it to the Kafka service in `.odctl/compose-kafka.yml`.
- A workspace made by `odctl init` with an earlier release keeps its old compose files, which publish on all interfaces and include port 29092. Run `odctl init --force` to copy the new files; it replaces your edits.
